input.quote: 5. Fees and Payment. The Parties agree to share any revenue generated as a result of this Agreement, or Customer's use of the Services or the Auction Platform, as set forth and detailed in each applicable Exhibit.
input.rationale: No minimum purchase, minimum spend, take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic binds AP anywhere in the Agreement. Economics run the other way: § 5 is a pure revenue-share in which Kubient collects from Advertisers and remits AP's share within seven days of receipt, and AP's only payment obligation is applicable sales/use taxes on its own use of the Services. There is likewise no volume cap or usage floor on AP: § 1 confirms the arrangement is non-exclusive and does not restrict AP from offering Inventory via other agents or selling to third parties, and the only "minimum" references are the Winning Bid Price floor that AP itself sets (p0014, in AP's favour) and Kubient's disclaimer that no minimum revenue level is guaranteed (p0062), which imposes nothing on AP. Services are engaged per Exhibit on a per-engagement basis, so AP pays/earns only on actual usage or ordered Services, satisfying the preferred position. Two points for the file, not deviations: § 4(a) gives Kubient all fees "generated" during the 90-day post-Initial-Term termination notice period, but that is revenue actually generated rather than a committed volume or penalty; and any future Exhibit could introduce a minimum, so Exhibit terms should be checked against this rule as they are executed.
